steps.text: Rhodes Island Landship
Common Rest Area Passageway

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Hrmm... Annie's off playing somewhere again...

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: And she didn't even bring me. Hrmph.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: I'll sort her out in short order.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Oh, a fork in the road.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: This way? Or that way?

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Oh, forget it. Let's go with the old standby.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: (Brings out a Victorian coin)

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Bena, Bena, oh lost Miss Prim♪ Where to go? Just listen to♪ him♪

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Here comes Sir Barkeley♪ The way is his whim♪

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Here!

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: (Tosses coin)

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: (Picks up coin)

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: This way, all the way, then. Hm-hm, very well.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: *sigh*—I can't believe there were spots this wonderful, and Iris never once mentioned them to me.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: She clearly doesn't know Rhodes Island as well as she says, does she?

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Aha! Found you!

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Annie, you little—

steps.name: Annie
steps.text: (Urging Bena to whisper)

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Annie
steps.text: (Pointing at the person in front of the TV)

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: (Whisper) Psst, what's she up to?

steps.name: Annie
steps.text: Playing a game.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: A game? Aren't games supposed to be like chess, and swings, and building sandcastles, and other such things? Is this a game too?

steps.name: Annie
steps.text: Mm.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Oh—

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: *shriek*! Did you just see a shadow pull someone off the screen into an alleyway?!

steps.name: Annie
steps.text: Mm.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: My word, Grandmother would be furious if she knew we were watching this sort of thing!

steps.name: Annie
steps.text: Mm.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Hmm, now...

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: I do slightly want to play.

steps.name: Annie
steps.text: Mm.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Aha, I knew it!

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: No wonder I couldn't find you.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Why don't you put a word in with the nice lady, then?

steps.name: Annie
steps.text: That'll scare her.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Will it?

steps.name: Annie
steps.text: It will.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Then you'll just have to allow me.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: After all, my play is your play.

steps.name: Annie
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Annie
steps.text: More power to you.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Oh, Annie, do you think I ought to put on a bit of a 'show' here?

steps.name: Annie
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Very well, as you wish.

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: (Almost at the final part. Still don't know if I can manage the true end.)

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: (I've gotten every collectible and every route, according to the guides.)

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: (Last step: beat the forced-loss fight.)

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: (I tried it while I was getting all the ending medals earlier, and couldn't pull it off.)

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: (I heard there was another phase transition to it, but I don't know if I can make it...)

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: (Takes off headphones)

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: H-Hello, did you need something?

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: (Uh oh, I'm not good with kids. This won't end well.)

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: What are you doing, Miss?

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: P... Playing a game.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: A game? I love games too!

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Can I play with you?

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: (Are all little kids so pushy these days?! Crap, what do I even do?)

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: (Can she actually play? Even if, I'm way into the endgame right now, and every enemy sucks to beat. I'm gonna feel terrible if she has a bad time and just drops the controller.)

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: Uh, um, er, this...

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Do you not like to play with others...?

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: (I—I-I-I-Is she about to cry?)

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: No—no, no!

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: We can play!

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Thank you, Miss, you're the best!

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: That's alright, heheh.

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: (Haven't I seen this kinda now-we're-friends scene in a dating sim before?)

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: (Whatever... I can just start a fresh run in a bit, since I've got the whole route down. Why not let her have a go—)

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: (No, wait!)

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: (This is an action-horror suspense game with @@, and ## and **! What was the rating, D or Z?!)

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: (I can't be letting a kid play this!)

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Miss?

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: Why don't we swap to another game, then? This one might be a little—

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: I want to play this one.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Can I?

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: (Please, please, pick up what I'm putting out!)

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: If you're 100% sure, then it's not—like you technically can't. But...

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Really?! Thanks, Miss!

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: Um?

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: F—For what?

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Do you use this control gadget to play?

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: Um, huh? That's—I meant—

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: And you press on these buttons.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Wow! A monster appeared!

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: What an impressively gaping mouth! How fearsome!

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: Uh...

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: Just let me have the controller a sec!

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: (Pause menu, Settings, Game Options, turn off Blood SFX—)

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: (—and most importantly, 'Disturbing Content': off!)

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Hrm? Why's the wide-mouthed fiend become so hazy?

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: Don't worry about it! Here's the controller.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Alright. Thank you, miss~

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: (This kid seems alright, aside from being so, um, forward. She talks sense, and she's sweet.)

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: (If all my friends were that polite when I was young, I wonder if maybe I'd be riajuu material now, like Utage?)

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: (Don't get carried away, Kirara. Like heck.)

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Hrmph, hah, hey!

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: (She's almost to the final set piece battle.)

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: (Come to think of it, I just taught her how to use a controller.)

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: (And I only figured that combo out not too long ago.)

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: (How'd she learn it?)

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: (Could I have unleashed a dormant gamer god?)

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: (Is there finally someone who could help me clear the secret set piece in Toukouden 2 Tachibana Edition?)

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: (Nnn... can't be sure yet.)

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: (Let's see if she can get past the set piece in Nukenin's hidden route first.)

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: (Sawara the Silentious. Pretty tough to beat.)

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Oh, there's an animation.

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: (Here it is, the nighttime Saeki Crossing!)

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Wh-Why can't I hack my way through?

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: I may be meant to flee.

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: (That's why people love Ringo Software. The way they connect and guide you through levels is so well-done, it clicks even for the littlest kids.)

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Ugh, how are there still monsters on the road? How obnoxious!

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: No rush, take it slow.

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: Careful. There'll be monsters from the car ahead and the stores streetside.

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: Right, right, right, for this set piece, you'll want to use the streetlamps to stall the big guy, if you can't afford to tank, and then you can sort out the mob.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Errm.

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: Use that big tornado move to clear them away a little.

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: But don't use it too much. Save some SP for the set piece.

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: (Can she understand what I'm even saying?)

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Step over here, and then—like that.

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: (Seems she does.)

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Wagh, this is a dead end!

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: But it's got some room to maneuver.

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: You're in the set piece battle now. That one's usually invincible, but you can sac an item from your inventory at him and his invuln disappears.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Which one?

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: This one, the 'Sachet of Consecration'. Equip to your inventory, then just use it like anything else.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Do I take aim at him?

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: Mhm. You've got one chance.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Very well.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: —A deadeye hit!

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: The invuln barrier's gone. Now slam him with everything you've got.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Very well!

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Waargh, what speed!

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: You can-NOT lose, okay? You only get to do this fight once per save, and losing means doing the whole thing over again!
Fifteen minutes later...

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: What do I do if I can't regenerate?!

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: Focus, he's low too!

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: Remember to evade and parry!

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: You can't block that one, jump away jump away!

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: Get him, get him!

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: Counter, nice! Chain a skill in!

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: Nice, nice, weak point! Hit it!

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Hei-yah!

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: Nice—niiiiiice!

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: You got the achievement—you got it, you got it!

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: G-Got what?

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: The true end!

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: True end? What do you mean, true end?

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Didn't I just start playing a short while ago?

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: That's 'cause I was already in the back part.

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: Oh, the staff credits are rolling, perfect. Let me tell you how the story goes in the first part of the game.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Very well.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: I can't read the words, after all. I've little choice but to rely on your narration...

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: (That's true, there's no Victorian release of the game. Impressive she had the patience to play for so long...)

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: Ahem. The game's called Nukenin, and it's about a nukenin—like the name—who left his homeland to live in a new nomadic city, and the story that happens there.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: What's a nukenin?

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: They're... um... the nu-keh part is runaway, the nin is... they're assassins, killers from the shadows, does that make sense?

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: And while this assassin was serving his master, uh, his lord, he saw his lord getting killed, and then was framed for the deed. So he had no choice but to leave the land for somewhere real far away.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: And then?

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: So then he's where the story takes place, Shin-Aki City.

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: The city's an actual real one. My super-riajuu friend Utage sent me a postcard from there once.

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: The biggest thing about it is—all the ghost stories. Plenty of ghost stories all come from there.

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: And most of them are from after the city got wrecked by a Catastrophe and rebuilt.

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: Like station stops that don't actually exist, this kinda mysterious guy where if you don't give him water he follows you all the way home and drinks all the water there, Aki figurines that like wandering out and calling their owners when they get lost and then find their own ways back, stuff like that.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: (You hear that, Annie? The next time you go out to play, remember to call me.)

steps.name: Annie
steps.text: (Yes.)

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: Really mystical ones, really especially scary ones.

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: Oh, the staff roll's over. Now it's mega-hyped secret ending time!

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: Mm...

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: Mmnn... mm?

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: Huh?!

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: Right, that had foreshadowing!

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: Oh my-Oh my god, everything makes sense now!!

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Miss, what was that animation afterwards about?

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: It all makes sense. You know how I just said the assassin moved to a new city? So, because he was such an expert at assassination and investigation, he started up this detective agency.

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: And the big guy we just defeated in that set piece was called Sawara the Silentious, the oldest ghost story of Shin-Aki City.

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: They say that at night, at the busiest crossing in the Saeki district, if you cross alone, you run into this Higashi ronin dressed in ancient clothes.

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: He uses sign language to ask you something, and if you can't answer him, don't respond or try to run, he'll hunt you down and kill you. You end up in the endless icefields, or he goes down.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: My, does that really happen?

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: I dunno either. Utage said the crossing in Saeki's all full of fun and excitement, and there's people drinking at every sake joint, and once they're done with one, they move onto the next, and then it's next morning and they just go back home and change clothes and go straight to work. Nobody's ever seen any kinda mute ronin.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Socky joint? They serve drinks and sell socks in your country?

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: Y—Yeah...

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: Anyway! This game's last hidden ending tells you that every ghost story in the entire city was descended from the oldest one, and then they spread out like tree roots.

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: Sawara wanted this Higashi place to become a city of ghost stories that outsiders would never see, and with that as his main thing, in the end he wanted to turn all of Higashi into a ghostly paradise!

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: Unfortunately, he met the protag, a guy from outside who probed out the whole thing.

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: In the end, Protag beats the original ghost story, finds out the city's secret, and the whole tree of stories falls apart, turning the city back to normal.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Simply because he won the 'set piece'?

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: Because ghost stories need enough mystery to last in people's minds. That's how they survive and get passed on.

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: If their true natures are revealed, the mystery disappears, and a million ghost stories lose their foundations all at once.

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: Their whole reason to exist is gone.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: (Oh? Oh-ho—)

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: (What a coincidence, I'd like a few things to 'last' in this lady's mind too.)

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: (Here's my plan of action.)

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: You seem very happy, Miss.

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: We beat the hidden route! No duh I'm happy! Super-happy, tera-happy!

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: Ahh—and I have no idea my new games are gonna get here—

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: I guess I'll head back to the dorms—

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Miss, might you wait a moment?

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: I'd like to tell you a story too. Would that agree with you?

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: You've told me so much, and I haven't given you one word. I feel quite awkward for that.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Oh, do wait a moment. You must be thirsty, Miss. I'll bring you a cup of water.

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: (Man, there she is... stepping up again...)

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: (What's going on?)

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: (Am I popular now?)

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Here's your water.

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: Thanks~

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: (Bait taken~)

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Well, then. Let me tell you a ghostly story of a Victorian city in exchange.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: As a...

steps.name: Annie
steps.text: (Thank-you.)

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Thank-you.

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: Oh, sure.

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: It's not everyday someone wants to talk to me.

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: Oh, yeah! I'm Kirara. What do you want me to call you?

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Can I tell you this tale before I answer?

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: Sure.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Hee-hee. Thank you, Miss.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: This story begins in Victoria, in a place named Lyndon—
It's raining again...
And I don't know where Mum and Dad are...
Oh, well. I needn't wonder about them. They don't mean as much as a bowl of hot soup would.

steps.name: Slum Dweller
steps.text: Hey, you Caprinae scamp. What are you hanging outside my door for?
Getting out of the rain. What else could I do?

steps.name: Slum Dweller
steps.text: Tch, you have the balls to sit right here when you can't even speak Victorian clearly? Go back to Leithanien where you came from.

steps.name: Slum Dweller
steps.text: Did you not understand me? Get lost, you're not welcome at my door.
I'm just sitting here to avoid the rain. I'm not coming inside your home.

steps.name: Slum Dweller
steps.text: Don't know when to give up, do you?! Bloody prick! I can handle a scolding from that bloody long-horns foreman, but you think you can talk back to me, you little shit?

steps.name: Slum Dweller
steps.text: Get out of my sight and never come back!
Urgh...
It hurts...
Let's shelter somewhere else...
If it comes to the worst...
Dropping from the city's edge... shouldn't hurt too much...
Hm?
Has someone fallen over there too?
It seems to be... an old lady?
Eek!
Granny, granny, are you alright?

steps.name: Old Granny
steps.text: Thank you, little lamb. There are so few children who would help an old lady up these days.

steps.name: Old Granny
steps.text: Oh, the children here. All they know is to ask me for apples. Not a soul in sight the moment I'd like a little help from them.

steps.name: Old Granny
steps.text: It's not often there's a child as kind to others as you. How good of you, how wonderful.
Granny, your clothes are dirty.

steps.name: Old Granny
steps.text: And yours, little lamb. Look, you've even gotten hurt here.
I'll be alright. It'll wash away in the rain.

steps.name: Old Granny
steps.text: You silly lamb. What if you caught a cold, drenched like this?

steps.name: Old Granny
steps.text: Hurry on back, now. I live quite close, and as rickety as I am, I can always make it home by myself.

steps.name: Old Granny
steps.text: Don't make your family worry.
I... haven't got one...
My Mum and Dad asked me to wait for them at a fountain square, and then I never saw them again.

steps.name: Old Granny
steps.text: Well, dearie me. Poor little lamb.

steps.name: Old Granny
steps.text: Coincidentally, I live all by myself, I do, and it's very lonely. Would you mind a bit of a chat with an old woman like me?
A chat...? I don't see why not.
(At least I can get out of the rain.)

steps.name: Old Granny
steps.text: Hoho, thank you, little lamb.

steps.name: Old Granny
steps.text: Erk...
What's wrong, Granny?

steps.name: Old Granny
steps.text: I'm old, is what it is. Beyond repair.

steps.name: Old Granny
steps.text: Little lamb, could I trouble you to carry my fruit basket for me?

steps.name: Old Granny
steps.text: It's all full of apples I picked not a bit earlier. Oh, slipping over, carrying this heavy basket all the while. My arms and legs just don't have the strength.

steps.name: Old Granny
steps.text: You're strong, little lamb. Could you help me?
I'll take over for you, Granny.
Say, Granny.

steps.name: Old Granny
steps.text: What is it?
Why would you go apple-picking on a rainy day? With rains as stormy as this, wouldn't it be better to stay in?

steps.name: Old Granny
steps.text: Hohoho, you don't understand, little lamb.

steps.name: Old Granny
steps.text: Only the apples washed by rain like this are the good, strong and sweet ones.
Granny, is this the place?

steps.name: Old Granny
steps.text: Yes, it is.

steps.name: Old Granny
steps.text: Just wait one moment. Let me find my key.

steps.name: Old Granny
steps.text: Here it is.

steps.name: Old Granny
steps.text: Come in, little lamb.

steps.name: Old Granny
steps.text: Welcome home.
Why, how warm!
A-And how pretty!

steps.name: Old Granny
steps.text: Hohoho, I do like hearing a little flattery every now and then.

steps.name: Old Granny
steps.text: Now just hold still.
Ah! My wound—it's stopped hurting?

steps.name: Old Granny
steps.text: Though I've not much ability to speak of, I can find it in me to heal the little scrapes.

steps.name: Old Granny
steps.text: Would you like to change into something pretty?
Mm-hm!

steps.name: Old Granny
steps.text: Then follow me, it's right upstairs.
It's so—dark in here.

steps.name: Old Granny
steps.text: This is where my darling granddaughter rests, after all.
Rests? Granny, weren't you the only person here?

steps.name: Old Granny
steps.text: Yes, I've always been the only 'person' here.

steps.name: Old Granny
steps.text: Come, meet my darling granddaughter.
This?
A doll? About as tall as me, and so finely detailed.

steps.name: Old Granny
steps.text: This is my granddaughter. Her name, you know, is Annie, an adorable Caprinae.

steps.name: Old Granny
steps.text: Just like you.

steps.name: Old Granny
steps.text: You see, I've always been looking for something, and today I finally found it in you, little lamb.

steps.name: Old Granny
steps.text: You've already helped so much. Granny is so very thankful.

steps.name: Old Granny
steps.text: Now, could you help me with one final thing?
Anything, Granny.

steps.name: Old Granny
steps.text: Oh, thank you, you darling little lamb.

steps.name: Old Granny
steps.text: Well, then, please, close your eyes.

steps.name: Old Granny
steps.text: Little lamb, now.

steps.name: Old Granny
steps.text: Take your delectable, kindly soul—

steps.name: Old Granny
steps.text: —and hand it out.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: They say there's been cases of orphan abduction like that all over Victoria.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Occasionally, someone sees the old woman taking away an orphan, and all say after that night, they never see the orphan again.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: As one might imagine, the policemen never found anything much. They'd go knocking, and find either there were no old people at that house, or it would just be empty.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Though, one wrinkle is that every home had a doll named Annie.

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: I-Is that the end?

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Yes, the end.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: What do you think, Miss Kirara?

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: I-It's pretty good.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: It's an old yarn in Victoria at this point. I hear the cities have several variations on it, like—

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: That's okay! Thank you!

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: If you're not fond of it, I won't tell.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: But, you know, no matter how the story changes, there's one thing that always stays the same.

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: Y-You can stop—I-I'm really not good with this sort of thing.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: But you're fine with it in a game?

steps.name: Kirara
steps.text: Playing a game is another thing!

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: That does make sense, I suppose.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: In that case—

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Annie, come say hello.

steps.name: Annie
steps.text: Hello, Miss Kirara.

steps.name: Annie
steps.text: I am Annie.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Hee-hee, that never stops being fun.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: What do you think? I'd say I was quite the performer.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Annie
steps.text: You went too far, Bena.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Oh, relax, you. I'll give Miss Kirara a proper apology later.

steps.name: Annie
steps.text: Also.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: What else could there be?

steps.name: Annie
steps.text: You forgot to tell her.

steps.name: Annie
steps.text: Your name.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: My word!

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Ugh, no need to get pernickety over that. I'll introduce myself when the time comes.

steps.name: Annie
steps.text: You made that up, just now?

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: That I did. I've got far better storytelling chops than Iris does, you know.

steps.name: Annie
steps.text: Granny will be upset, telling stories like that.

steps.name: Annie
steps.text: You didn't make her evil enough.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Excuse meee—? Was that not evil enough? I think I've already made Grandmother out to be plenty rotten.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Oh... now that you say it, I suppose I can see it lacking a little.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Grandmother told me at first, if I'd run off with that basket that day, those five apples would've been my very last meals.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: And that wicked trap after she led me into the dining hall, then went to take a bath and change. If I so much as took a bite of the feast in there, I'd be sent right back out onto that stormy street before I could blink.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Now that was certainly real. I remember it even now.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: That left some very murky shadows on my young heart!

steps.name: Annie
steps.text: What Granny says is the truth.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: I wouldn't say she's rotten, otherwise!

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: I haven't even a clue how Granny first entered the Castle of Dreams.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Perhaps because she was a bad good person.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Just like me.

steps.name: Annie
steps.text: You're not bad.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Hrmph. What makes you think to try and grovel to me now?

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Be good and confess, Annie. Did you or did you not play this game beforehand?

steps.name: Annie
steps.text: I did.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Then what was on your mind, dragging me here too?

steps.name: Annie
steps.text: I played it before. It was fun.

steps.name: Annie
steps.text: I wanted you to play it too.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: I see, I see. So that's why the game controls felt so familiar to me.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: How many hours did you spend on it?

steps.name: Annie
steps.text: Three nights, twenty-four hours.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Twenty-four?! Did you sneak out at bedtime? Grandmother really will be mad!

steps.name: Annie
steps.text: I have you. I'm not scared.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Hm...

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Come over, Annie.

steps.name: Annie
steps.text: Mm.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Here, sit by my side.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: We may have just passed this level, but we haven't touched the previous one at all.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Teach me very carefully, one-on-one, okay?

steps.name: Annie
steps.text: Mm.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: And another thing. What did Miss Kirara mean with the 'set piece' she kept going on about?

steps.name: Annie
steps.text: Boss.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Oh, so that's all it was. And here I thought it was some strange new thing.

steps.name: Annie
steps.text: It's started.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Oh, yes. Let's focus on the gaming, now.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: What would you say? Do you think our scaring of Miss Kirara might really take root in her country, sprout forth into a new 'ghost story,' perhaps?

steps.name: Annie
steps.text: Focus, Bena.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: O-Oh, very well. Sorry.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: It's a push of this button, isn't it.

steps.name: Bena
steps.text: Game, start.
